title: Have I Seen This Before?
description: A Bloom filter is a set that never stores what you put in it — thirty-two bits and nothing else. It can tell you for certain that something was never added, and only ever tell you that something probably was. Watch a name it was never given come back as a yes.
long_description:
A Bloom filter answers one question, have I seen this before?, and it answers it without holding on to anything you gave it.

Adding a name runs it through three hash functions and sets the three bits they land on. Asking about a name runs the same three and reads them. If any one of them is 0 the name was definitely never added. If all three are 1 the filter says yes — but those bits could have been set by three different names that have nothing to do with the one being asked about.

That is a false positive, and the wall ends on a real one. The three hash functions are FNV-1a, djb2 and sdbm, the bit positions are whatever they actually produce, and the name that comes back wrongly is found by asking the filter rather than drawn in.
action_hints: slow it down to follow one name through its three hashes
pause on the false positive at the end
deal new data and watch a different name collide
